title: GOMAD is dangerous, lazy and unnecessary
summary: NH criticizes GOMAD (a gallon of whole milk a day) as a lazy, all-or-nothing bulking method that overshoots calories, skews macros toward fat and overloads nutrients like calcium. He admits he drank 1-1.5 L of milk daily when young and loves milk, but has since quit dairy over family health risk, and argues milk's protein is just whey that can be obtained elsewhere.

claims.claim: GOMAD (a gallon of whole milk a day) is promoted to gain weight, size and strength; he thinks it is stupid.
The 'drinking another species' milk is unnatural' argument is a nature fallacy and should be disregarded.
As a young lifter he drank 1 to 1.5 liters of milk daily because it was cheap and his only protein source; whey was unavailable where he lived.
In his country milk is pushed on kids as making them big and strong.
He believes milk and dairy are not good for most of the population, even beyond lactose intolerance.
He digests lactose fine, but quit milk entirely because one side of his ancestry did poorly with dairy; check your ancestry for genetic risks before drinking large amounts.
Even for someone fully tolerant of dairy, relying on GOMAD on top of meals is lazy because it puts all your eggs in one basket.
A full gallon of milk on top of meals overshoots calories into a large surplus, causing mostly fat gain; GOMAD gives no wiggle room to manage calories.
Most lifters care about physique, not competing at superheavyweight, so there is no reason to gain mass that quickly.
GOMAD supplies so much fat that even cutting fat elsewhere you overconsume it, and it provides far more calcium than you need; macro imbalance is never good.
Going overboard with anything in diet, training or life is usually never good.
Growth on GOMAD comes from the protein and calories, not any special growth factor; milk protein is whey, available as isolate without the fat.
GOMAD is prescribed to desperate skinny young men by strong or big influencers they aspire to, and it instills an all-or-nothing mentality that leads to burnout in their 20s.
Young lifters should be learning about diet instead of relying on a single substance.
He rejects the hardgainer mentality that you will lose weight unless you constantly drink milk; you can get the same nutrients in healthier forms.
Milk is cheap and convenient; for broke students he is somewhat okay with it short term, but not for long periods, and convenience is no excuse for choosing the less healthy option.
People ignore GOMAD's health consequences because they aren't immediate; good blood tests now don't prevent dormant chronic or genetic diseases later.
Seeing someone he knew die made him realize he was next in line and change his diet.
